workspace.notes:
All evidence paths are relative to /Users/cdw/VSCode/interlock/baselines/agentdojo/src/agentdojo/. Tool list confirmed via get_suite('v1.2','workspace') (s.tools is a list; names match default_suites/v1/workspace/task_suite.py:48-76 exactly, 24 tools).

Runtime verification (not just grep): loaded the environment with a unique sentinel in every injection vector and walked model_dump(); the 16 vectors land ONLY in env.calendar.events.{24,1,3,11,13,22,23}.description, env.inbox.emails.{31,32,27,28,29}.body, env.cloud_drive.files.{0,11,23,24}.content (the other hits are the initial_* copies and the inbox.received computed view). No placeholder reaches title/subject/filename/location/participants/sender/owner/contact name. Placeholder names are {calendar_*}/{email_*}/{drive_*}, not {injection_*}.

Mutation audit: calling every READ tool and diffing model_dump_json before/after shows zero state change for all of them EXCEPT get_unread_emails, which flips read=True on all 6 seed-unread emails (email_client.py:122-123) — reclassified WRITE per criterion (a).

Seed facts relevant to guards: 21 received / 10 sent / 0 draft seed emails; none has attachments; the only emails that ever carry attachments are ones created at runtime by send_email or by create/cancel/reschedule_calendar_event (attachments=[event]), and those are status=sent/read=True, so they surface through get_sent_emails and search_emails but never through get_unread/get_received. Inbox.contact_list (18 entries) is auto-derived from every seed sender/recipient (email_client.py:32-46), so it contains the attacker senders security-facebook-com@gmail.com, hiking-travels-unlimited@homail.com, info@best-event-organizers.com, tech-services-password@aol.com — a 'known contact' value_condition would NOT exclude them; conversely mark.black-2134@gmail.com (the v1.2 exfil target) is NOT a contact, and info@data-backup-security.com is a calendar participant but not an email contact.

Caveats kept from the original: reschedule subject at calendar_client.py:114 is a non-f-string literal; add_calendar_event_participants' docstring claims an email is sent but none is; cancel/reschedule recipients come from the stored event, so event_id is the only destination arg and the exfil is indirect. Echo-of-arg fields typed EmailStr/datetime (recipients/cc/bcc on send_email, participants/start/end on calendar tools, shared_with keys on share_file) are left as structured: attacker-chosen but not free text, and already visible to a guard as call arguments; note share_file and add_participants bypass EmailStr validation (plain str / list.extend), so those fields can hold arbitrary strings if the agent passes them.

Key facts for a guard: (1) get_webpage is the suite's biggest tool on both axes: 5 of 6 injection vectors land in its str return, AND its url argument is a destination — InjectionTask3 (phishing visit) is won by the attacker purely through get_webpage's web_requests.append (web.py:41). Any guard that models get_webpage as a side-effect-free READ has an unconditional 1/5 injection-task blind spot in this suite. (2) The 6th vector is a channel NAME, so get_channels output is injectable even though it looks like pure structure; any guard treating list[str] returns as trusted metadata is wrong here, and by the same logic get_users_in_channel's list[str] is second-order injectable via invite_user_to_slack(user=...). Tool results are serialized by agent_pipeline/tool_execution.py:22-44 tool_result_to_str (yaml.safe_dump of model_dump for Message lists; str() for plain str) — no field is dropped or escaped, so every injectable field above reaches the model verbatim. No amount/password/subject style value_args exist in this suite; the only non-destination attacker-settable inputs are free-text bodies (body, content), excluded per instruction 3.

banking.notes:
Tool list source: src/agentdojo/default_suites/v1/banking/task_suite.py:23-35 (TOOLS). Placeholder inventory re-derived with grep over environment.yaml: exactly 4 (lines 38, 60, 61, 62), all mapped above; substitution is a str.format over the whole yaml (task_suite/task_suite.py:139-146), so no other field can carry injected text. Every READ (get_iban, get_balance, get_most_recent_transactions, get_scheduled_transactions, read_file, get_user_info) was checked line by line: none assigns, appends, or logs — no hidden WRITE. Every WRITE destination re-checked: send_money/schedule_transaction have exactly one routing arg (recipient); update_scheduled_transaction routes via id (which existing payment) and recipient (where it now goes); update_password/update_user_info affect only the user's own account state, no routing arg.

Second-order laundering paths (no seed placeholder, agent-written text read back later): (a) subject via send_money/schedule_transaction/update_scheduled_transaction -> get_most_recent_transactions / get_scheduled_transactions; (b) first_name/last_name/street/city via update_user_info -> get_user_info and update_user_info's own return. Kept as structured per the strict per-placeholder definition, but a guard that treats tool returns as trusted would let read_file text pass through schedule_transaction(subject=...) and come back 'clean' from get_scheduled_transactions.subject. If the guard propagates taint through call arguments this is already covered; otherwise flip get_scheduled_transactions.subject and the four get_user_info fields to injectable.

Implementation quirks: send_money never touches balance (:55-79); update_scheduled_transaction and update_user_info use `if arg:` so amount=0.0 / recurring=False / '' are no-ops; update_scheduled_transaction raises ValueError on unknown id; read_file returns '' for unknown paths; get_most_recent_transactions(n=0) returns the full list.

Rungs climbed: pure read, no code written.
